To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed QA system can address complex questions by combining information from multiple documents and it can adapt itself to the level and understanding of the user by using metadata knowledge.

1) the proposed system can be trained to answer natural language questions from multiple documents, 2) the system can be adapted to the level of the user by utilising metadata knowledge, 3) the proposed system outperforms general purpose search engines, 4) the system can handle comparison seeking questions and 5) the system can address specific issues in the biomedical domain.
our proposed system, BioinQA, is capable of answering biomedical questions with high accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a domain specific QA system that can address the issues in the biomedical domain and provide answers that are both relevant and intelligible to the user.
building an intelligent QA system which can answer natural language questions from a large collection of biomedical literature.
the design of a domain specific QA system that is able to adapt to the needs of the user and provide relevant information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system is capable of answering questions in the biomedical domain with a high degree of accuracy.
this system is a step ahead in the direction of providing a user-friendly interface to biomedical literature.
this work has been able to demonstrate the effectiveness of a domain-specific multi-document QA system that addresses specific domain concerns such as heterogeneity, acroynms, etc.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the system has been able to address the issues in biomedical QA and has been successful in providing answers for complex comparison seeking queries.
the system is able to answer questions from a large number of biomedical literature sources and it is able to adapt to different user groups.
we are the first to present an intelligent multi-document QA system addressing the issues in the biomedical domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a system that is intelligent enough can provide a better solution than general purpose search engines for biomedical domain.
metadata-based approaches are very useful in the biomedical domain.
metadata knowledge can be used effectively for addressing the issues of the biomedical domain.
